architecture.mechanism: Machine learning-based supercapacitor (SC) current reference generation using an LSTM neural network to dynamically offload high transient loads from the battery, reducing peak battery current, peak power demand, and battery energy consumption, which improves thermal performance and reduces battery stress.
architecture.intervention: Integrate a supercapacitor module into the hybrid traction battery pack of the 2020 Toyota Camry with an LSTM-ONNX-based controller that predicts and supplies transient current demands, offloading high-frequency/high-magnitude current pulses from the Li-ion battery cells to keep cell-level thermal load within safe limits prior to thermal runaway.
architecture.expected_effect: Lower peak battery current, lower I²R heat generation within battery cells, smoother current ripple, and reduced battery temperature rise during high-load driving (e.g., 65 mph cruise with transient accelerations), which suppresses the thermal events that precede under-vehicle smoke/fire originating from the traction battery pack.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument the Camry hybrid traction battery pack with cell-level thermocouples and current sensors, then run a controlled drive cycle (e.g., IM240 and EUDC equivalents at 65 mph with transient load steps) with and without the LSTM-controlled supercapacitor offload active; the mechanism is falsified if pack cell temperatures do not show a statistically significant reduction (e.g., <5% peak temperature reduction) or if peak battery current is not measurably reduced, since the paper reports 21.3–33.5% peak current reduction and thermal improvement as the mechanistic effect.
